summary: A 1970 note by T. Schipper about reallocation in case of an input error. It concerns how space allocated for incoming data is handled when something goes wrong.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 71 describes how the UCLA CCN host handles an input error that makes a message's length unclear. It stops more traffic on the link, waits for the sender's return message and then issues a new allocation.

subtitle: A procedure for clearing a link after an input error.

tldr.problem: An input error may prevent the receiving NCP from determining the message length, leaving the link's flow-control state unclear.
tldr.mechanism: If it can identify the link, the receiving NCP sends GVB with frac=0, ignores further messages on that link, waits for RET and then sends a new ALL.
tldr.outcome: The receiving host knows the link is clear before issuing a new allocation.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 71 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC describes a procedure for the UCLA CCN host dated 25 September 1970.

sections.title: When an Input Error Hides Message Length
sections.content:
The note says an input error while reading a message from the IMP may make it impossible for the receiving NCP to determine the message length. It presents a procedure for the UCLA CCN host to resynchronize flow control.

The procedure applies when the NCP detects an input error and can identify the intended link number.
sections.plainLanguage: If an input error hides where a message ends, the receiving system may not know the link's state. The note gives a way for the UCLA CCN host to clear that link before continuing.

sections.title: Stop, Wait and Reallocate
sections.content:
The receiving NCP sends GVB with frac = 0 to the sending host and disregards further incoming messages on that link. If the sender is not waiting for an RFNM, it sends RET immediately.

If the sender is waiting for an RFNM for the errored message or a following message, it waits for that RFNM before sending RET. After receiving RET, the receiving side sends a new ALL.
sections.plainLanguage: The receiver asks the sender to stop and ignores more messages on that link. It waits for RET, including any pending RFNM, before issuing a new allocation.

sections.title: Confirm the Link Is Clear First
sections.content: The order of operations matters: the receiving host waits until it has received RET before sending a new ALL. The note says this ensures the link is clear before the new allocation is issued.
sections.plainLanguage: The receiving host does not allocate the link again until the sender confirms it is clear. This keeps the two sides' flow-control state aligned.
